thread.title: Why Warren Buffett has doubled down on Apple: Its fans are ‘psychologically and mentally’ locked in

author: Luke Stangel
title: Why Warren Buffett has doubled down on Apple: Its fans are ‘psychologically and mentally’ locked in
text: – Contributing writer Feb 26, 2018, 1:20pm CST Warren Buffett may not be an Apple Inc. customer (he famously still carries around a flip phone), but he is one of the company’s most bullish investors. Asked why in a CNBC interview on Monday, he said Apple (Nadsaq: AAPL) had an “extraordinary consumer franchise” that locks consumers in “psychologically and mentally.” “I see how strong that ecosystem is, to an extraordinary degree,” Buffett said. “You are very, very, very locked in, at least psychologically and mentally, to the product you are using. [The iPhone] is a very sticky product.” Buffett’s investment holding company, Berkshire Hathaway Inc., ended 2017 holding $28.3 billion worth of Apple stock — its second largest holding, behind Wells Fargo & Co (NYSE: WFC). “If you look at our holdings, you would assume we like [the companies we invest in] in the order they rank by dollar value of holdings,” Buffett said. “But if you look at them in terms of recent purchases over the last year, we’ve bought more Apple than anything else.” Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK) began buying Apple stock in early 2016, back when the stock hovered around $100 per share, and hasn’t stopped. The investment firm amassed some 165.3 million shares as of the end of 2017. Berkshire Hathaway is now Apple’s fourth-largest institutional investor. That marks a reversal for Buffett, who had famously avoided buying technology stocks, preferring instead to buy shares in companies with predictable revenue and easy-to-understand business models. Buffett has long had an appetite for financial stocks: Wells Fargo, Bank of America Corp., American Express, U.S. Bancorp, Moody’s, Goldman Sachs and Bank of New York Mellon are among his 15 biggest holdings. He also has big stakes in two airlines, Southwest Airlines Co. and Delta Air Lines. One of his most famous investments, Coca-Cola, is now only his fourth-biggest holding. He also owns stock in Charter Communications. In Buffett’s eyes, Apple is far closer to a blue chip stock like Coca-Cola than it is to a hot tech company like Tesla or Facebook. Over the years, the legendary investor has promoted his investments by taking reporters to Dairy Queen, drinking Coca-Cola on camera and handing out boxes of See’s Candies at events. In Monday’s interview, Buffett said Apple CEO Tim Cook once asked him why he hadn’t upgraded his flip phone to a new iPhone yet. “Well the answer is just I'm out of touch,” Buffett quipped. “But I tell Tim, ‘As long as I haven't gotten one, the market is not saturated.’ The day I buy one, there is probably nobody left after that.”
